title: The TELCoMB Protocol for High-Sensitivity Detection of ARG-MGE Colocalizations
author: Bravo, Slizovskiy, et al.
materials: MEGARes database FASTA and CSV files

steps.title: Install Conda
steps.instruction: If Conda is not already installed, download the appropriate installer for your OS (e.g., for an M‑series MacBook use https://repo.anaconda.com/archive/Anaconda3-2023.07-2-MacOSX-arm64.pkg) with wget -O conda.pkg <URL> and then run installer -pkg conda.pkg; alternatively install via the Anaconda website.

steps.title: Create TELCoMB environment
steps.instruction: Create a new Conda environment named telcomb that includes snakemake and git from the conda‑forge and bioconda channels, activate it, and clone the TELCoMB repository.

substeps.instruction: conda create -c conda-forge -c bioconda -n telcomb snakemake git

steps.title: Create directory structure
steps.instruction: Within the cloned repository create the sample directory (and, on a cluster, a logs directory) required by the workflow.

substeps.instruction: mkdir -p telcomb/logs                 # only needed on a Slurm cluster

steps.title: Link FASTQ files
steps.instruction: Create symbolic links (or copy/move) of all FASTQ files into the sample directory; replace the placeholder path with the actual location of your FASTQ files.

steps.title: Combine FASTQ per sample (optional)
steps.instruction: If a sample has multiple FASTQ files, concatenate them into a single file using the cat command; this assumes each sample’s files are in a dedicated sub‑directory.

steps.title: Link concatenated FASTQ (optional)
steps.instruction: After concatenation, create a symbolic link to the combined FASTQ file in the TELCoMB sample directory.

steps.title: Edit config.json defaults
steps.instruction: Open telcomb/config/config.json and set the following keys as needed (the defaults are shown).

substeps.instruction: "WORKDIR"   : "test_dir",       # where all output will be written
"LONG_READS" : "true",          # set to false for short‑read data
"DEDUPLICATE" : "true"          # keep true for higher quality; set false only if deduplication makes the run too long

steps.title: Prepare Slurm environment (optional)
steps.instruction: If running on a Slurm cluster, load the Conda module, edit the run script header and the Slurm profile configuration with your account and email information, and ensure the logs directory exists.

substeps.instruction: module load conda   # if a Conda module is available

steps.title: Verify parameter settings
steps.instruction: Review telcomb/config/config.json to confirm input/output locations and, for colocalization analysis, ensure the gene‑fraction cutoffs are set to 0.80 for resistome (ARG) and 0.50 for mobilome (MGE) as described in the protocol.

steps.title: Launch workflow
steps.instruction: Run the TELCoMB pipeline either locally (optionally inside a screen session) or on a Slurm cluster by submitting the run.sh script.

substeps.instruction: screen -S telcomb   # start a detached screen (optional)

steps.title: Review standard outputs
steps.instruction: After the workflow finishes, examine the generated files and figures, including read‑length JSONs, duplicate FASTQ (if DEDUPLICATE=true), read‑length histograms, and summary CSVs for resistome and mobilome features and richness.

steps.title: Review colocalization results
steps.instruction: Inspect the colocalization‑specific output files produced by the overlap and find_colocalizations rules:

substeps.instruction: Overlapping MGEs CSV (SN_DS_overlapped_mges.csv) – lists MGEs that exceed the overlap threshold and are excluded from downstream analysis.

Colocalizations CSV (SN_DS.fastq_colocalizations.csv) – rows contain read/contig ID, ARG header, ARG positions, MGE header(s), and MGE positions; defaults require ≥80% ARG genome fraction, ≥50% MGE genome fraction, and co‑occurrence on the same read/contig.
Genes List Excel (SN_DS_genes_list.xlsx) – intermediate list of reads with ARGs and associated MGE information.
Colocalization Richness CSV (SN_DS.fastq_colocalization_richness.csv) – unique colocalizations with gene group, MGE gene, distance between genes, and occurrence count.
Colocalization plot SVG (SN_colocalizations_plot.svg) – visual representation of each ARG‑MGE colocalization per sample.
